seo_title: Homeowners Need More Touchpoints Before Hiring
title: Why Homeowners Take Longer to Decide
content:
###  **A Small Number With Large Consequences** 

LocaliQ reported that customer touchpoints before converting increased from 4.9 to 5.5. 

That looks minor written down. In practice it means a homeowner now needs, on average, more than five separate encounters with a company before hiring it — and that most contractors are budgeting for fewer. 

###  **Why the Number Went Up** 

Homeowners are doing more research than they used to. Industry surveys consistently find that the large majority read reviews before choosing a contractor, and most compare several companies before calling any of them. 

Rising costs have made the process more deliberate. Housecall Pro found that 77 percent of homeowners are delaying or scaling back projects even while 96 percent still plan to spend on their homes. More deliberation means more contact required before a decision. 

###  **What This Does to a Single-Channel Strategy** 

If a homeowner needs five or six encounters and your company only appears in one place, you are relying on that channel to produce all of them. Very few channels do. 

An ad seen once is one touchpoint. A search result they scrolled past is arguably not even that. 

###  **Where the Missing Touchpoints Come From** 

This is the practical argument for presence rather than campaigns. A homeowner who has seen a company's vehicle on their street, spoken with someone from it at their door, and later finds a complete and well-reviewed Business Profile has accumulated several encounters without the company paying for each one separately. 

###  **The Reframe Worth Making** 

It is tempting to judge any single marketing activity by whether it produced a call this week. On a five-touchpoint average, most individual encounters will not — and cannot. 

The question is not whether a given conversation closed. It is whether the company is accumulating encounters faster than competitors are.
